question: In which of the following decade only, India’s Population had shown negative growth?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1911-1921.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The decade 1911-1921 was the only period in India's recorded history when the population showed a negative growth rate.**
 
• **This negative growth was primarily due to the influenza epidemic of 1918, also known as the Spanish Flu, which caused significant mortality.**
 
• **World War I (1914–1918) also contributed to the disruption of resources and widespread hardships, worsening the population decline.**
 
• **During this period, India witnessed widespread famines and epidemics, which significantly impacted the population.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1901-1911:** This decade saw positive population growth despite challenges like famines. The census recorded steady growth due to improved administrative measures and better infrastructure.
 
• **1921-1931:** This decade marked the beginning of steady population growth. Post-1921, India experienced improvements in healthcare and sanitation, which contributed to a rise in population growth rates.
 
• **1931-1941:** The population continued to grow during this period due to advancements in medical facilities, improved public health measures, and agricultural developments despite political unrest during the independence movement.
 
• **Spanish Flu:** A global pandemic that significantly impacted India during the 1918-1920 period, leading to millions of deaths and contributing to the negative growth rate in the 1911-1921 decade.
 
• **Famines:** India faced several famines during the British colonial period, including the Great Bengal Famine of 1943. However, the specific famines during the 1911-1921 decade contributed heavily to population decline.
